CHashMapCalculateHash semantics (stubbed with FNV-1a on both arms): the real hash at 0x1eeb88 is strlen + murmurhash 0x1eea84, NOT what this arm computes, so the BUCKET LAYOUT it produces is the stub's, not the device's. Every positional claim about the map in this receipt is therefore about the probe logic, which is the body under judgement, given a deterministic hash.
CHashMap::Insert semantics (stubbed identically: linear probe from hash&mask): it defines the post-grow map, and only the ORDER and the VALUES handed to it are real evidence
ShowMessage semantics (stubbed): the tail jump is modelled as a call then a return, so "does not return" is not itself tested

device behaviour: this is a synthetic-memory oracle over the original bytes, not execution on a phone
not_applicable: Variable_GetName_Scope 0xd2494 (count < count-1) is unreachable for any count that is not INT_MIN; it is documented, not translated, and no case can reach it without staging an inconsistent map header whose result would be a NULL dereference in both arms
the same body's "< 0 slot" test is done with `bmi` AFTER the gate-1 branch, so a gate-1-closed call never evaluates it - that ordering is covered, the "skip" it implies is not a separate decision
F4's `beq` on count == 500 means count > 500 would append out of bounds; count only moves by +1/-1 in this body, so that state is unreachable and is not staged
the 16 B entry's +0xd..+0xf padding is never read or written

F3's reverse scan with map->count > the number of hash>0 entries: the inner walk is unbounded (0xd236c only checks hash and j), so that state reads past the array and its answer is not a property of the body

findings: Variable_Global_Init has no idempotence guard at all: the second call re-runs ReAlloc and clears the table again.  The arm calls it once per case, so this is read off the bytes (no compare/short-circuit instruction exists between 0x1f3354 and 0x1f33b0), not off a re-execution test.

DoVariableInstanceExists answers "is the tag different from 0x00ffffff", not "does the name exist".  Two cases make the difference concrete: an unset tag answers 0 even though the name resolved, and the Direct-returns-early path (inst+0x24 == 0) answers 1 because the RValue it just zeroed is not the sentinel.

Variable_GetName_Scope folds type > 100000 into the instance domain unconditionally (`orrgt`), and the boundary is STRICT: type == 100000 is refused while 100001 is accepted.  Two cases pin the boundary from both sides and tooth f3_normalize_ge proves a `>=` would be caught.

The local function table read names[slot] with no bound check.  The arm turns that from a card note into an observation: a count of 4 with 8 live names answers "l5"/"l7", and adding the check breaks two cases (f3_local_bound_check_added).

Variable_BuiltIn_Add writes the entry BEFORE it touches the map and bumps builtin_numb LAST, so no reader can ever see a map value pointing at a half-built entry.  The order is visible in the trace (0x1f4e38..0x1f4e40 then 0x1f4ea0/0x1f4f00, then 0x1f4f28) and tooth f4_count_two moves the count without moving anything else.

The 4th argument of Variable_BuiltIn_Add is genuinely dead: the differential varies it (p3) and gets a byte-identical record, and the writable bit is computed from the setter instead.  This is the third independent confirmation of the card's claim (card §6, the 7 inconsistent call sites, and now an executed case).

The probe compares key POINTERS, not strings.  Case "the same bytes at another address" yields two table entries and two map entries, and tooth f4_key_content_compare (pointer -> strcmp) is caught by exactly that case.

card/byte agreement: every instruction of the four bodies was re-read from the pinned image for this run; see card_deltas for the single documentation glitch (a truncated pool address, no behavioural content).

NEW (not on any card): the instance map reverse scan has NO bound on its inner walk.  0xd236c advances the entry cursor until it has counted i+1 entries with hash > 0 and then compares that entry; if map->count ever exceeded the number of hash>0 entries, the cursor would run past the entries array and read unowned memory.  The fixture therefore always stages count == the number of occupied entries, which is what makes every map case in this arm terminate inside the array.  The original's behaviour in the out-of-step state is undecidable from these bytes alone - it depends on whatever follows the array.

card_note: All four cards (cards/Variable_Global_Init.c, cards/DoVariableInstanceExists.c, cards/Variable_Misc.c) were re-checked against llvm-objdump for this run: instruction counts (24+2, 33+0, 158+13, 164+6), every pool word value, every branch target and every GOT addend agree with the bytes. No card claim in this module had to be overruled. The items the cards mark open are handled as follows: Variable_Misc open 1 (names[slot] has no bound check) is now an OBSERVABLE in the arm - the fixture stages 8 names behind a count of 4, and the tooth f3_local_bound_check_added proves a translation that added the check would be caught. Variable_Misc open 2/3/4/5/6/7/8 are untouched: they are about who reads the tables and what the enumerations mean, which no case in this file can decide. Variable_Global_Init open 1 (what one globdecl byte is) stays open; the arm only pins that exactly 10000 bytes are written per call.
